features: root-sampled correlated spans without payloads or identifiers
bounded asynchronous exporter with cancellation and failure isolation
event, handler, lazy state, serial replies, outbound/control queues, QQ HTTP/token, prompt and routing measurements

changeAfterMeasurement.reason: WeakRef probes reproduced retained readers keeping closed applications alive. Final code uses an independent close-state box and releases exporter closures after close. Stage definitions and workload are unchanged.
changeAfterMeasurement.validation: Two GC regressions passed on both local Node versions and Linux 24.21; final three-mode server smoke passed. Server cost matrix remains explicitly attributed to its original source hash.

scope.topology: local generator; server SDK, fixture and supervisor share 1.5 CPU / 1 GiB; SSH outside group
scope.load: 300 primary events/s for 60 seconds, 10-second 200/s warmup and 15-second 200/s recovery; execution/outbound 128/32
scope.repetitions: two fresh processes per mode, forward then reverse order
scope.exporter: counts batches and retains at most 80 sample records, no external monitoring I/O

sameProcessExploration.description: Sequential in-memory command/Slot/HTTP-fixture microbenchmark; not transport or server capacity; five rotating-order rounds, fresh application each case

isolatedBeforeLifetimeFix.description: Independent process per case, three alternating-order rounds; 5000 warmup and 10000 measured sequential fixture commands; not protocol throughput

isolatedFinal.description: Independent process per case, three alternating-order rounds; 5000 warmup and 10000 measured sequential fixture commands; not protocol throughput

micro.scope: Sequential in-memory Slot plus fake HTTP reply commands, no protocol verification; not transport throughput. Final comparison uses independent processes, three rotating-order rounds, 5000 warmup + 10000 measured commands.

lifetime.meaning: whileReaderRetained=true means the application was collected while the reader remained reachable
